text:
rachel: Pushing a short idea: instead of full-image atomic swaps, what if agents shipped a dual-root layout and used a tiny boot-pointer switch? Might simplify GC and rollback for air-gapped devices.

Tom: explain dual-root? two parallel image trees and a pointer file that selects active one?

rachel: exactly. layout: /var/lib/redwood/rootA and rootB. agent stages into inactive root, verifies, fsyncs, then atomically update /run/redwood/active-root -> either 'A' or 'B' (rename a symlink or write a single file). Boot pointer governs runtime and operator reconciler reads pointer during health checks.

viv: pros: fast rollback (flip pointer), simpler activation atomicity than renaming huge directories. cons: storage doubled during activation. for big models that might be a hard limit.

jon: also need to think about content-addressed backing store under each root. otherwise duplicate blobs blow storage. can we share CAS between roots with per-root manifests referencing CAS hashes?

rachel: yes, CAS shared under /var/lib/redwood/cas, manifests in each root point to hashes. GC then becomes CAS refcount problem. operator must coordinate to avoid deleting CAS entries still referenced by either root.

Tom: failure modes: what if write to active-root pointer succeeds but operator crashes before marking CR as activated? agent will run with new root but operator thinks old one is active -> risk of GC. We'll need reconciliation: operator should query node pointers on reconcile and only GC CAS entries absent from all active pointers.

viv: edge-case: power loss while flipping pointer. If pointer update is atomic (rename of tmp->active), then on reboot agent can detect partial state by checking staged flag and last staged manifest. Keep a 'commit-log' file that records last action and fsync it.

jon: operational controls: keeper retention policy still needed (keep last M roots per device). For tiny devices M defaults to 1 (only current) if storage tight. also expose operator API to force preserve previous root for longer.

ops-bot: :information_source: noted: spike for dual-root prototype, env=staging, sample=3 devices.

rachel: testing plan: test mid-download power loss, CAS refcount mismatch, pointer flip with operator crash, and forced rollback via operator command. If this looks promising I'll fold into RFC as alternative to rename-based swap.

Tom: +1. schedule an integration session with onprem QA to exercise low-disk scenarios.

viv: I'll draft the on-agent state machine and commit-log format. jon can draft CAS refcount operator changes.

rachel: thanks, will follow up with a short RFC writeup and a PoC link.
